label: No Vote Under Twenty-One
detail: The 26th Amendment is never ratified, so citizens aged 18 to 20 cannot vote for president in 1972.
assumption: Adults aged 18 to 20 (8.1% of adults 18+ in the 1970 census [I]) are removed from the electorate in every state; the backbone has no age split, so they are taken as a uniform slice of every cell, voting like the rest of it. Young voters in fact turned out less and leaned further toward the challenger.
facts_text: The proposed amendment lowering the voting age to 18 failed to win ratification by the states, and the minimum age for voting for President remains 21 in nearly every state.
Citizens aged 18 to 20 are not on the registration rolls for the November 7 election.
research_questions: How did voters aged 18 to 20 split between the two major candidates in 1972 compared with older first-time voters?
What was the turnout of 18-to-20-year-olds in 1972 relative to those aged 21 to 24?
In states that already allowed voting before 21, such as Georgia and Kentucky, how did young voters behave in earlier elections?
